To be fair,

Crude oil is the input, Diesel/Gasoline/others are the refined product.

PRIMARILY what is shipping through Hormuz is Crude oil, not Diesel or Gasoline.

The Crude is being shipped to refineries to be turned into Diesel.

Russia has Crude and refineries, so they can make Diesel at home, just like USA. So Treasury allowing Russia to sell Diesel is different.

You have to have Crude and refineries OR you are buying Crude to be refined in your refinery.

Hope this helps.

AI Overview

Major oil refineries are located in the countries that border the Strait of Hormuz and the adjacent Persian Gulf.
The primary nations bordering or immediately surrounding the Strait of Hormuz with significant refining infrastructure include:
• Saudi Arabia: Operates massive coastal and regional processing complexes, including the Ras Tanura refinery (roughly 550,000 barrels per day of capacity) and facilities in Al Jubail.
• United Arab Emirates (UAE): Features the massive Ruwais refinery (over 840,000 barrels per day), one of the largest single-site refining complexes in the world, as well as facilities in Jebel Ali, Dubai.
• Iran: Houses major domestic refining hubs along or near the Gulf coast, such as the Abadan refinery (360,000 bpd), the Persian Gulf Star gas condensate refinery (450,000 bpd), Isfahan, and Bandar Abbas.
• Bahrain: Operates the Sitra (Bapco Energies) refinery, with a capacity of around 380,000 to 400,000 barrels per day.
• Qatar: Hosts large energy and condensate processing and LNG infrastructure centered around Ras Laffan and Mesaieed.

Normally, about 750,000–1 million barrels of diesel/gasoil pass through Hormuz daily—roughly 32–42 million U.S. gallons. These are pre-disruption estimates, not today’s actual flow. spglobal.com

About 250,000 barrels daily—10.5 million gallons—normally goes to Europe. That’s roughly 25–33% of Hormuz diesel shipments and 6% of Europe’s road-diesel demand, using pre-disruption estimates.

Directly to the EU and UK: effectively zero under import bans. reuters.com
Before sanctions, Europe imported approximately 610,000 barrels daily of Russian diesel in 2022—about 26 million gallons, over twice its normal Hormuz supply.
